title: Beer & Charcuterie Board
seo_title: Beer and Charcuterie Board for 8–12: Shopping List & Pairings
description: A beer and charcuterie board for 8–12: sharp cheddar, smoked Gouda, pepper jack, Gruyère, summer sausage, pretzels, pickles and mustard, matched to beer styles.
hook: Built for a cooler of beer: sharp cheddar for the IPA, smoked Gouda for the dark beer and pepper jack for the lager, plus pretzels, pickles and two mustards.

items.name: Smoked Gouda · porter or smoked beer

why: Beer pairs with cheese differently from wine. Its bubbles scrub fat off the tongue, and hops and roasted malt can stand up to strong flavors. A hoppy IPA meets sharp cheddar, a crisp lager cools the heat of pepper jack, and a dark or smoked beer echoes smoked Gouda.

The meats are the hearty, smoky kind that suit beer: summer sausage, brisket, salami and pepperoni. Salty pretzels, dill pickles and pickled jalapeños make it pub food, and the two mustards tie the meat and pretzels together.

timeline.what: Take the cheddar and Gruyère out of the fridge.
Take out the smoked Gouda and pepper jack.
Take out the meats; slice the baguette and pumpernickel.
Place the cheeses with the mustard bowls in the middle; fan out the meats.
Fill the gaps with pretzels, pickles, almonds and grapes; open the beer.

faq.q: Which beers go with this board?
faq.a: Four styles cover it: an IPA for the cheddar, a porter or smoked beer for the Gouda, a lager or pilsner for the pepper jack, and a Belgian-style ale for the Gruyère.

faq.q: Can I serve it without beer?
faq.a: Yes. Hard cider or sparkling water with lemon both work, because the bubbles do the same job as beer's carbonation.

faq.q: How many people does it serve?
faq.a: 8 to 12 people on an 18–22 inch board.
